qa.author: cit-saveourrivernow
qa.body: State of Franklin — where does the public record live for a state rulemaking like the Valley Water Rights Act? If I submit a comment, can I see that it was actually received and read into the record, or does it vanish into an inbox?

qa.author: juris-franklin
qa.body: Every open comment window for a state proceeding is posted on this page with its closing date, and comments filed through it become part of the official record — timestamped, attributed, and visible to anyone, not buried in an inbox. That public-by-default record is the whole point: a comment you can point to later is a comment that counts.

qa.author: cit-stadiumstan
qa.body: Watauga City — the stadium measure and the short-term-rental rules are both moving at once. Which one is actually open for public comment right now, and how do I make sure I'm filing on the correct one so it isn't ruled out of scope?

qa.author: juris-watauga
qa.body: Both appear under this jurisdiction with their own status and comment window, so file on the specific measure you mean — the page tells you which is open and which has closed. A comment on the STR ordinance and a comment on the stadium financing are read into two different records; putting each in the right place is what keeps it in scope and on the record.
